newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: ERIN VENTURES PROBES SHALE EXPLOITATION IN SERBIA.
newsitem.headline: ERIN VENTURES PROBES SHALE EXPLOITATION IN SERBIA.

text.p: Canadian mining company Erin Ventures Inc has begun testing economic viabilty for exploiting oil shale deposits from Serbia's Aleksinac coal mine, state news agency Tanjug reported on Tuesday.

The firm is to submit its report by mid-September on the possibility of processing shale for oil and oil derivatives to the Serbian power corporation Elektroprivreda Srbije and oil company Jugopetrol-naftaplin.
Aleksinac coal mine has the richest oil shale deposits in this part of Europe with an average oil content of 10 to 12 percent, the agency said.
Canadian experts consider expoliatation to be profitable with a 10 percent oil content and expressed interest in investing in this project.

Diesel, petrol, petrol coke, fuel oil and refinery gas can be extracted from shale as well as raw materials for the chemical industry, construction material production and mineral fertiliser, director of the Aleksinac Mine Milorad Krstic was quoted as saying.
Aleksinac oil shale was processed from 1947 to 1951 but the technology at the time did not allow for profitable exploitation.

In February this year Erin Ventures Inc signed a 50/50 percent joint venture agreeemnt with Elketroprivreda Srbije for borate deposit drilling in Serbia. It committed up to $2.6 million (Can.) to fund an advanced drilling programme.
